ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the attached figure is a schematic diagram of sea-level pressure distribution near the southern tip of South America and Antarctica. The figure has meridians such as 30°W, 60°W, and 90°W and latitudes such as 30°S and 60°S. “Ushuaia” is marked near the southern tip of South America, and multiple isobars are also drawn in the figure. The isobars and pressure values have no direct effect on the calculation of day and night length in this question; the image mainly provides the background that Ushuaia is located at a relatively high latitude in the Southern Hemisphere. Then reason: the stem gives that sunset in Ushuaia by local time is 20:00. In local solar time, noon is 12:00, and sunrise and sunset are symmetrical about 12:00, so the day length in Ushuaia = 2×(20:00-12:00)=16 hours, and the night length = 24-16=8 hours. Mohe is about 53°N, close in latitude value to Ushuaia at 54°S and opposite in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres; on the same date, the lengths of day and night at similar latitudes in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres are complementary, therefore Mohe’s day length on that day is approximately equal to Ushuaia’s night length, namely about 8 hours. Mohe local solar time sunrise = 12:00-8/2=8:00. Mohe’s longitude is 122°E, 2° east of Beijing time’s standard meridian 120°E, so local time is about 8 minutes earlier than Beijing time, therefore Beijing time is about 7:52, approximated as 8:00.

The longitude of Mohe is 122°E, 2° east of the Beijing Time standard meridian 120°E, so local time is about 8 minutes earlier than Beijing Time; therefore Beijing Time is about 7:52, approximately taken as 8:00.
